vision: Pilgrimage runs stay deterministic and responsive even when multiple browser clients (keepalive + screenshots + captures) are active: control never silently detaches from the live game, objective distance keeps progressing, and startup stalls no longer force manual reruns.
objectives: Eliminate the intermittent startup/control stall seen in screenshot-enabled runs by preventing observer/snapshot clients from stealing or nulling the active game control channel.
Make relay ownership fail-safe: when the current game client disconnects, ACT/INTERACT routing must automatically hand over to another eligible live game client without dropping the control loop.
Expose bridge session diagnostics (active game session id/label + handoff events) in OBS/events so controllers and playtests can detect and explain routing transitions.
Harden run tooling so visual snapshot processes are explicitly non-controlling observers (or bridge-disabled), while the keepalive gameplay client remains the sole controller.
Validate with seeded pilgrimage runs (including screenshot-enabled mode) that quest_completed is reached without prolonged no-progress startup phases.
implementationHints: Treat this as one cohesive reliability pass across relay + game client + playtest tooling; avoid ad-hoc one-off fixes in only one layer.
Keep protocol changes backward compatible by adding optional HELLO/OBS fields rather than breaking existing payload shapes.
Prefer deterministic ownership rules (explicit role/mode + clear failover) over timing-dependent heuristics.
implementationDetails: In agentBridge/wsRelayServer.js, replace single mutable gameConnection pointer with tracked game peers metadata (connection id, role mode, lastSeen). Add deterministic active-controller selection that excludes observer clients.
Define HELLO extensions for game clients (e.g., clientLabel/sessionId/mode=controller|observer). Observer/snapshot clients may send OBS but must never become ACT targets.
When active controller disconnects, immediately promote the best remaining eligible game peer and continue routing ACT/INTERACT/CAPTURE/EDIT without requiring reconnect/manual rerun.
Emit bridge lifecycle events/metadata into OBS stream (e.g., bridge_controller_acquired, bridge_controller_lost, activeControllerId/label) so playtest logs can prove ownership transitions.
In src/agentBridge/config.js + client.js, add opt-in controls for observer/disabled bridge mode via env/query flag; ensure normal gameplay client defaults remain unchanged.
Update scripts/visual-snapshot.cjs (and run-agent-exploration.sh wiring if needed) so snapshot tabs launch in bridge-disabled or observer mode and cannot preempt control ownership.
Update scripts/browser-client-keepalive.cjs and/or run scripts to provide stable controller label/session metadata for deterministic relay selection and easier diagnostics.
Extend scripts/playtest-beacon-pilgrimage.mjs diagnostics for no-progress startup detection (objective distance unchanged + ACT sent) and record controller ownership signals when stalls are avoided.

Validation before handoff: npm run build passes; run seeded pilgrimage checks including ROAM_SEED=404 in both screenshot-disabled and screenshot-enabled profiles; each must reach quest_completed with OBS/ACT healthy and without prolonged static-distance startup state (>6s).
Record concrete evidence in exec_result.json: relay ownership logs/events, exact commands used, and at least one screenshot-enabled successful run artifact path.
